messages:
mira-support: FYI - AcmeMaps hitting repeated 503s and p95 tail timeouts starting ~10:12 UTC. Customer trace id: trace-1a2b3c4d. They see gateway 502/504 and logs show 'request queue depth exceeded' + continuous-batcher backlog growing. They just flagged this as P1 with support.
thomas-sre: On it. Can you paste the trace + tenant id? I'll pull queue metrics.
mira-support: Tenant: acmemaps-prod. Trace: trace-1a2b3c4d (attached in DM). Customer says degradation coincided with a batch import job hitting our API at ~10:10.
kaira-eng-runtime: @thomas-sre quick hypothesis: continuous-batcher KV cache spin-up under tenant spike -> hot KV misses -> queue pile-up. If queue depth hits max, we early-reject which shows up as 5xx gateway errors.
thomas-sre: Pulling metrics now: enqueue_rate spike at 10:09 -> sustained for ~6m. Queue depth hit 8192 for a few shards, p95 tokens exploded. Continuous-batcher backlog latency correlates.
thomas-sre: Running quick query in console:
```
SELECT sum(enqueued) as enq, max(queue_depth) as depth
FROM ingress.metrics
WHERE tenant = 'acmemaps-prod' AND ts >= 1748499600
GROUP BY minute
```
-> shows enq spike 3x baseline and depth peak 8192.
olivia-product: Customer is on hosted tier with burst allowed but no reserved capacity. They report this impacted interactive users - they lost map tile generation calls. We've got a customer meeting in 45m.
mira-support: Customer asked for mitigation steps. Any quick mitigations we can suggest while we triage?
kaira-eng-runtime: Short-term: advise them to split the import into smaller concurrent windows or throttle to <50% of prior peak. Platform-side: we can temporarily increase request_queue_max_depth for their tenant (unsafe but quick) or route them to a lower-cost, higher-concurrency variant. Also can enable prefix KV pre-warm for their model.
thomas-sre: Before we change configs, I want to reproduce locally. Can someone drop the exact request pattern? jason-customer sent an example: heavy concurrent POST /v1/generate with long sequences (~8k tokens) and one-off bulk uploads.
jason-customer: Confirmed - we started a bulk migrate that used 60 parallel workers. We thought API would autoscale. We can pause if needed.
kaira-eng-runtime: Repro steps for internal repro (posting here):
```
# simulate tenant burst
for i in {1..60}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \ 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
    -d '{"model":"longseq-2", "input":"<~8k tokens>"}' &
done
```
Watch batcher backlog and kv miss rate.
thomas-sre: I ran a smoke repro in staging with 40 workers and saw kv-cache miss rate -> coldfill thrash -> continuous-batcher queue linger -> dequeue stalls -> 502s. Repro successful :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: alert - autoscaling policy adjustment rolled (policy-id: pol-984) by thomas-sre for temporary burst mitigation. No prod code changes.
thomas-sre: Mitigation applied: bumped tenant queue depth cap from 8192 -> 12288 and temporarily relaxed batcher dequeue timer to reduce thrash. Monitoring now.
mira-support: I told customer we've applied a temporary mitigation and asked them to resume one worker at a time to validate. They will respond in 10m.
jason-customer: Resuming now with 10 workers. Initial results: still some 503s but much better. We'll scale slowly and report.
olivia-product: Let's schedule follow-up: tech-runbook update + recommend docs for tenants on bulk imports (best practices + pre-warm). I'll own the customer postmortem and credits if needed.
kaira-eng-runtime: Action items: (1) Add KV pre-warm toggle for tenants running bulk imports (2) Add soft-queue throttling when batcher coldfill rate > X (3) Create alert for continuous-batcher backlog growth + KV miss correlation. I'll open tickets.
thomas-sre: I'll revert temporary queue cap after 2h and watch for regressions. Creating a post-incident trace with graphs in #incidents. Marking P1 -> P2 if stable for 30m.
mira-support: Customer confirmed stable after 25m. They've lowered concurrency and will run the rest overnight. Closing immediate escalation — moving to postmortem. :white_check_mark:
